messages.subject: shinyGridster?
parts:
Hi

There are a couple of threads regarding the flexible grid version... can you clarify what is the status of the gridster version and what plans there are for it?  It's great, obviously, one wants to use it when there's a beta.  Thanks.

Giles

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: shinyGridster?
parts:
Hi Giles,

I'm not sure how much time Winston plans to expend maintaining shiny-gridster, but I expect he'll be able to chime in on that.

As one alternative, I've been working on ShinyDash (https://github.com/trestletech/ShinyDash), which was initially a fork of Winston's shiny-gridster work. It's basically a rewrite of Winston's initial prototyping but uses Rickshaw instead of HighCharts (to maintain MIT licensing) and then adds a few new widgets/extensions. You can see an example here: http://spark.rstudio.com/trestletech/ShinyDash-Sample/

I'll let the other authors speak to the plans of their Shiny Gridster packages, but I do plan to continue development on this package and maintain it. Ultimately, we'll be releasing it on CRAN once it's stable.

Jeff

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: shinyGridster?
parts:
Another package making use of gridster, and built on top of Winston's ideas is dashifyr.

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/ramnathv/dashifyr

Dashifyr integrates seamlessly with rCharts, which provides access to multiple JS charting libraries, including Highchart and Polycharts. By design rCharts exposes the complete API of the charting libraries, implying that any chart you can create in JS, you can create using rCharts, and hence include in dashifyr.

I do plan to release it on CRAN, but it might take a bit longer, since I need to put rCharts on CRAN first. However, a stable version will be maintained on github and questions addressed.

Hope this helps.

Best,
Ramnath

messages.subject: Re: shinyGridster?
parts:
Hi Giles -

I made shinyGridster as a demonstration of how to package up Javascript libraries for use with Shiny. The code in shinyGridster is very simple (not counting Gridster itself, which I didn't write), and it should be perfectly usable as is. Are there any more features that you're looking for from it?

Jeff's ShinyDash is meant to be a generalized dashboard solution, if that's what you're looking for.

-Winston
